No a.e. isomorphism chart joins a point of E_0's axis to a point of an E_kappa (notMem_axis_of_isAEChart), so every such chart, either way, has a regular source and is a chart isomorphism (chartIso_models_none_some, chartIso_models_some_none). The argument is causal and uses no holonomy or developing map: J^-(p) of a BTZ point lies on the axis (defi:causal_E0, l.1345-1347; E0.le_axis_iff'); every point of E_kappa, the line included, is the limit of regular points g(u) = (tau - u, (u/2) e^{i0}) that all lie in the causal future of g(eps) inside the regular part; and J^+ is closed in E_0 (E0.isClosed_Jplus). The source brunswic2021cauchy's prop:isom (BTZ_1.tex:378-383, alpha = 0 or beta = 0) also gives it, and ETT does not cite it here.

ETT.tex:1396-1406, 1408-1417, 1419-1428 at E_0-manifolds (every singular point a BTZ point, in a chart into E_0), with every model of E_{>=0} admitted as a chart target: the natural causality exists, is unique among absolutely minimal causalities with an isomorphic chart at each point, is causally arc-connected and has push-up. No hypothesis is left in the readings DEC-25, OQ-18, OQ-34/35, OQ-64, OQ-82 (massA_dec25_e0_manifolds). It is the causality of BPrimeE0.existsUnique_causality_e0 (A = {0}). So for E_0-manifolds the causality generated by the X_A-atlas (def:singular_spacetime, l.1501-1504) is the same for A = {0} and A = [0, oo). The three corollaries are not refuted there.

kb_proposals: The E>=0 family's singular structures are Causal.MassAModelsInstance.massAModelSingularGX, a named global instance by cases on o, equal by rfl to E0GX.singularGX at none (massAModelSingularGX_none, the h0 of BPrimeE0.hiso_massAModel_none) and to EAlphaGX.singularGXFamily kappa at some kappa. hreg at every model: hreg_massAModel.

The family instance fires only for a variable o. At a fixed model, MassAModel none or MassAModel (some kappa) reduces to E0 or Massive kappa.1 before instance search, and synthesis fails. Statements at a fixed model need a section with attribute [local instance] E0GX.singularGX (or EAlphaGX.singularGX, EAlphaGX.singularGXFamily). Inside a proof, use letI := massAModelSingularGX (some kappa) before any lemma whose implicit instance argument is a fixed model (IsAEChart.trans, chartIso_of_isAEChart_of_subset_reg with Y a fixed model). A type ascription that mentions a fixed model fails for the same reason; leave it out (have h := hf.symm.trans he).

No a.e. isomorphism chart joins E_0's axis to an E_kappa: Causal.MassAModelsInstance.notMem_axis_of_isAEChart. The proof is causal, not holonomic: J^- of a BTZ point lies on the axis (E0.le_axis_iff'), J^+ is closed in E_0 (E0.isClosed_Jplus), and a radial static curve in E_kappa approaches the line from a regular point. Consequences: (b') E_0 <-> E_kappa (hiso_row_none, hiso_column_none) and E_0-manifolds natural over the whole family (massA_dec25_e0_manifolds). (b') over MassAModel now owes only E_kappa <-> E_kappa' at sources meeting the line (hiso_massAModel_of_sing, forall_exists_massA_models_iff_sing).

To make an a.e. isomorphism chart a ChartIso on the regular part of its source, restrict it with isAEChart_restrOpen (IsRegularOn.mono on both sides) and apply chartIso_of_isAEChart_of_subset_reg. The restriction's coercion is the chart's by rfl (OpenPartialHomeomorph.coe_restrOpen).

A causal curve in E_kappa that stays off the line: tau -> (tau, Cone.polar ((t - tau)/2, theta)), 1/2-Lipschitz by Cone.dist_mk and Cone.dist_of_same_dir. Do not use staticLe_of_ball near the line: its ball around the start point contains the apex.
